title: OpenDoc Reader download manifest
description: Describes everything the app may download on first run (llama-server builds and model files, each pinned by SHA-256) and the rules the hardware suggester applies. Every downloaded file is verified against its sha256 before use. See docs/architecture.md and ADRs 0007 and 0008.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editors.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this manifest format. Increase it only for changes the app must handle explicitly.

runtimes.description: Runtime binaries the app downloads and runs.

models.description: Downloadable models, keyed by model id. The id is stable and is what the suggester rules and the app settings refer to.

id.description: Lowercase identifier made of letters, digits, dots and hyphens.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file as published.

backend.description: The llama-server backend the app would use on this machine.

llamaServer.description: The pinned llama.cpp release that provides llama-server. Pin the bNNNNN build tag; the GitHub Latest release can have no binaries.

build.description: The llama.cpp build tag, for example b11669.

license.description: SPDX license identifier of the runtime.

builds.description: Builds keyed by <os>-<arch>-<backend>, for example windows-x64-cuda. The app picks one from the hardware probe.

files.description: Every archive needed for this build. All of them are extracted into the same folder. CUDA builds need the cudart archive in addition to the main one.

tier.description: The user-facing tier the model belongs to.

experimental.description: True for models offered only as an advanced option and labelled experimental in the UI.

engine.description: Id of the engine in the Python engine that drives this model (see engine.capabilities).

license.description: SPDX license identifier of the model weights. Shown to the user before download.

sources.description: Repositories the files come from, each pinned to an immutable revision. Most models have one; a PaddleOCR pipeline combines several model repositories.

revision.description: Full commit SHA of the Hugging Face repository.

dir.description: Optional sub-folder of the model folder to store the file in. Used where several files must share a directory, for example one folder per PaddleOCR model.

role.description: model is passed to llama-server with -m, mmproj with --mmproj. paddle-model is a file of a PaddleOCR inference model that the Python engine loads from its dir.

urls.description: Download URLs in the order to try them: Hugging Face first, ModelScope mirror second when the same repository exists there. All URLs serve the same bytes, so one sha256 covers them.

requirements.description: Measured or estimated needs, used for fit badges and the Setup screen. See the model notes for how each figure was obtained.

minVramMB.description: VRAM needed for full GPU offload, rounded up from the measured peak. 0 for models that run on the CPU only.

minRamMB.description: System RAM (unified memory on Apple Silicon) needed to run on the CPU.

backends.description: Backends the model is expected to work on.

llamaServerArgs.description: Arguments appended to llama-server; empty for models that do not use it. The app adds -m, --mmproj, --host 127.0.0.1 and --port itself, and adds -ngl 99 on GPU backends or -ngl 0 on the CPU backend. Always pass --port, because the default changed between builds.

notes.description: Provenance, caveats and where the figures come from.

range.description: Inclusive numeric range. Give min, max or both.

when.description: Conditions on the hardware probe. A rule matches when every condition present holds; an empty object always matches. The probe reports 0 for a quantity that does not apply: vramMB is 0 on the cpu and metal backends, unifiedMemoryMB is 0 except on Apple Silicon (where ramMB equals it).

backend.description: Matches when the selected backend is any of these.

suggester.description: Rules for the hardware suggester (ADR 0008). Rules are evaluated in order. Code only evaluates them, so tuning needs no code change. Keep this language small.

defaultModel.description: Model id recommended when no recommend rule matches.

recommend.description: Ordered. The first rule whose when matches picks the recommended model.

model.description: Recommended model id; must exist under models.

reason.description: Plain-language reason shown to the user. May use the placeholders {gpuName}, {vramGB}, {ramGB} and {unifiedGB}, which the app fills from the probe.

badges.description: Ordered. For each model, the first rule whose models list contains it and whose when matches sets its fit badge. A model with no matching rule gets wontFit.

models.description: Model ids the rule applies to; each must exist under models.

badge.description: runsWell: Runs well. slow: Slow on this PC. wontFit: Won't fit. hidden: the model is not offered on this machine.
